<!--
Measured, not read: a table's rows are double spaced by default, the body's
spacing, in every format, and a cell that wraps is spaced as its rows are
(but in .docx, whose wrapped lines stay single). APA lets a table body be
single, one-and-a-half or double spaced; table-spacing asks for the others
(tests/layout-table-spacing-single.qmd), and journal and doc modes take
single (tests/layout-table-spacing-journal.qmd).

The formats had each spaced rows their own way: the .pdf at the body's
double spacing, 24pt; typst with Typst's five points of padding, 18pt, while
a cell that wrapped took the body's 24; .docx 23pt; .html 37pt. Now the rows
stand 24pt apart in the .pdf and typst, Word's 27.6pt in .docx, and 2 lines
in .html.
-->

| Headword | Column B                      |
|:---------|:------------------------------|
| Rowone   | 1                             |
| Rowtwo   | 2                             |
| Rowthree | Wrapone a cell long enough that it has to run on to a second line inside its column of the table wraptwo |
| Rowfour  | 4                             |
